Statistics Canada tables on Indigenous peoples, by subject

Source: R/src.R
indiex.Rd

The tables of the project's open data service that hold what is most often asked for about First Nations people, Metis and Inuit: health indicators, perceived mental health, wellbeing, suicidal thoughts, the census counts of population and of households, life expectancy and infant mortality. indiex() finds the tables of one subject among those indtabs() lists, and with load = TRUE loads the first.

Usage

indiex(
  name = c("health", "mentalhealth", "wellbeing", "suicide", "censuspop", "censushh",
    "lifeexp", "infantmort"),
  load = FALSE,
  base = getOption("crimlab.data", "https://data.crimlab.dev")
)

Arguments

name

The subject: "health", "mentalhealth", "wellbeing", "suicide", "censuspop", "censushh", "lifeexp" or "infantmort".

load

TRUE loads the first table found, with odtab().

base

The address of the service, or of a mirror of it (a folder holding manifest.json and <db>/<table>.csv.gz, which may be a file:// address). The default is getOption("crimlab.data"), or the project's service when that is not set.

Value

The rows of indtabs() for the subject; with load = TRUE, the first of those tables as a data frame.

Details

The package holds no data: the tables are Statistics Canada's, mirrored by the service under the Statistics Canada Open Licence and loaded and checked by odtab(). A subject is matched by words in a table's description, so a table the service adds later is found without a new release; a subject with no table there gives a data frame of no rows.

Errors: name not one of the subjects; load not TRUE or FALSE; with load, a subject with no table; those of indtabs() and odtab().

References

Statistics Canada. Indigenous Population Profile, 2021 Census of Population. Ottawa.

Statistics Canada. Statistics Canada Open Licence. https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/reference/licence

See also

indtabs(), odtab(); sctidy() and scests() to read a Statistics Canada table once loaded.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# needs the internet
indiex("mentalhealth")[, c("key", "rows")]
x <- indiex("lifeexp", load = TRUE)
} # }
try(indiex("weather"))
#> Error : indiex: `name` must be one of "health", "mentalhealth", "wellbeing", "suicide", "censuspop", "censushh", "lifeexp", "infantmort", not "weather".
